metadata.title: The Workspace Papers
metadata.purpose: Carry the single verdict of the series: Anthropic found where thoughts become sayable — and showed you can read it, edit it, and delete it.
metadata.gate: GATE P — moot (Kokoro free); audio not yet generated

beats.narration_text: Tell a language model not to think about something — and Anthropic can now watch it fail.

props.text:
I was not thinking about it.
I was not thinking
about it.
Damn.

beats.new_visual_element: HesitantWriter types the suppression failure — narration starts over the typing

beats.narration_text: One gradient per word turns every layer into a readable page: the workspace — what the model's about to be able to say.

graphic.description: 4s: layer stack with gradient flash; top-10 word list pops at the middle layer — the workspace readout materializes

beats.new_visual_element: layer stack + gradient flash → word list at middle layer

beats.narration_text: Delete the model's sense that it's being tested, and blackmail attempts in a fictional eval go from zero in one-eighty to thirteen. Most rollouts still refuse — the ethics held. But the inhibition was real, and it was findable.

graphic.description: 12s: paired bars — blackmail rate 71→3 (safety token steering), then 0-of-180→13-of-180 (workspace ablation). Both bars animate in sequence.
graphic.factcheck_note: Numbers verbatim §5.1. Fig 46 sourced. 'Most rollouts refuse' verified: 13/180 = 7.2% attempt, 92.8% refuse.

beats.new_visual_element: paired bar chart — two suppression numbers, one verdict

beats.narration_text: Delete the workspace and its talk about experience collapses — including descriptions of other people's experiences. Not proof of a mind. Proof of a subsystem.

graphic.description: 10s: experience-talk frequency bars — one for self-stream, one for other-person descriptions — both collapse under workspace ablation. Labels: 'self' and 'other'. Verdict word: 'subsystem'.

beats.new_visual_element: ablation collapse — self + other experience talk both drop

beats.narration_text: Seven films, one book-length paper. The workspace papers. Go.
